research_question.research_question: How are automation, AI, and digital technologies transforming marketing and sales practices, and what benefits, challenges, and limitations does this bring?
research_question.core_relation: the adoption/integration of AI and automation technologies (ML, chatbots, programmatic advertising, IT-marketing collaboration) as drivers of change in marketing and sales functions (personalization, brand management, customer value, consumer wellbeing)
out_of_scope: consumer wellbeing psychology as standalone topic
financial performance metrics unrelated to marketing
research_question.note: The seeds coherently cluster around AI/automation's impact on marketing and sales, though a few (consumer wellbeing, entrepreneurship, edge computing) sit at the periphery rather than the core.

prompt_template:
Research question against which relevance must be judged: {rq}

Core relation at the heart of the question: {core}
Clearly in scope: {ins}
Adjacent but NOT the core: {outs}

For each publication below, assign a single relevance score from 1 to 10 based on its title and
abstract. Judge each publication on its own -- do not revisit earlier scores and do not compare
publications against each other. Parallel LLM models apply these same criteria.

Relevance Score (1-10):
1-2: no material connection to the research problem -- different field, unrelated phenomenon, or
     pure methodological/technical noise.
3-4: very weak connection -- addresses the broader field or context in which the problem sits, but
     not its central dependency.
5-7: connected -- concerns related constructs, neighbouring variables or partial aspects of the
     problem, but the link is indirect or incomplete.
8-9: directly relevant -- explicitly studies the dependency or phenomenon at the core of the problem.
10:  fully relevant -- a core study of exactly the stated problem, with empirical evidence.

Where only a title is given and no abstract, score what the title supports and set "title_only": true.

Publications to score (each numbered):
{items}

Output format: return ONLY a JSON array, one object per publication, in the same order as the
numbering. Do NOT reproduce the publication text -- give only the number (id) and the score:
[{{"id": int, "Relevance_Score": int, "title_only": bool}}]
validation: On 302 iteration-1 records the haiku>=5 gate lost 0 of 90 full-ensemble includes; two-stage vs 3-model kappa=0.935.
